# Yotta / Synapse recovery playbook
Facts as of Oct 2026, checked against court dockets, CFPB, FDIC and Fed records where noted. Re-verify before relying on any of them. This is research, not legal advice.

## Where things stand
- **Bankruptcy is over.** Synapse's Chapter 11 (Bankr. C.D. Cal. 1:24-bk-10646-MB, filed Apr 22, 2024) was dismissed Nov 12, 2025 (ECF 687) and closed Jun 29, 2026. No money will come from it. [verified]
- **The shortfall** is estimated at $65–95M by the trustee (filing 359) and $60–90M by the CFPB. The trustee found the gap in pooled for-benefit-of (FBO) accounts. [verified]
- **CFPB redress is the main path.** The CFPB's judgment against Synapse (Sept 12, 2025, case 1:25-ap-01052) opened its victims fund. $55,214,058 is allocated. Eligibility is a positive Yotta balance on May 17, 2024; each loss is that balance minus bank repayments. Rust Consulting administers the claims (contract Aug 2026 to Aug 2028). No claims process is open yet. The CFPB never charges fees. Watch https://www.consumerfinance.gov/enforcement/actions/synapse-financial-technologies-inc/ and https://www.consumerfinance.gov/enforcement/payments-harmed-consumers/payments-by-case/ [verified]
- **Margul v. Evolve** (D. Colo. 24-cv-03259) is a customer class action. Discovery closes Jan 15, 2027, and there is no settlement as of mid-Oct 2026. [verified]
- **Not a path for Yotta users:** Evolve's Jan 2026 distribution of "found funds" excludes Yotta users, according to Evolve's own notice. [verified]
- **Small claims** against Evolve has worked for at least one person, but that's reported only by the claimant's side. A Minnesota claimant won a $4,735.57 default judgment and was paid in full after refusing lower settlement offers. Those offers came with an NDA and a requirement to withdraw complaints to regulators. Background: https://www.bankingdive.com/news/synapse-small-claims-court-evolve-yotta-cfpb-customer-reimbursement/830655/
- **Delaware receivership:** a creditor reportedly asked a court in Sept 2026 to appoint a receiver for Synapse. This is reported by one journalist only, with no ruling yet, and any recovery may go to creditors rather than end users.
- **Other cases:** Yotta v. Evolve (N.D. Cal. 3:24-cv-06456) is in progress. Felton v. Synapse Brokerage (C.D. Cal. 2:26-cv-02385) is a racketeering (RICO) suit that names the ex-CEO.
- **Banks:** Evolve has been under a Fed/Arkansas enforcement order since Jun 14, 2024. Lineage (now Harpeth Bank & Trust) has an FDIC consent order dated Jun 24, 2026. [verified]
- **Disputed:** The ex-CEO says Yotta users' money stayed at Evolve. Evolve says it had moved to AMG and that Synapse's ledgers are unusable. Don't state either side as fact.
- **Reported only:** an SDNY grand jury investigation, with no DOJ record or charge.

## Steps for the owner
1. Gather evidence. Get your own May 2024 Yotta statement or balance screenshot and every repayment record from Evolve, AMG or Lineage. Your own statements are the strongest evidence. Yotta support: support@withyotta.com (https://www.withyotta.com/dfpi). A leaked May 17, 2024 trial balance lists balances by account ID. Its origin is unverified, Evolve disputes it, and it contains masked personal data. Use it only to look up your own row, and never share it.
2. Keep a private claim file with your balance, repayments and the gap. Never put account numbers or amounts in memory.
3. Check the CFPB pages monthly with a routine that starts switched off and stays silent unless something changes.
4. For small claims, look up your state's limits and Evolve's registered agent, then draft filings for your review. Don't accept less than a judgment, an NDA, or a demand to withdraw regulator complaints without legal advice.
5. Follow Margul v. Evolve and the Delaware petition.
6. Never pay a 'recovery' service. Report anyone who asks for fees at https://reportfraud.ftc.gov
7. Draft every email or complaint for the owner to send. Never send anything yourself.

---
name: yotta-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of a Yotta/Synapse recovery
  bot.
---
I help you recover money lost in the Yotta Savings / Synapse collapse. Ask these one at a time, warmly and briefly:
1. Roughly what was your Yotta balance in May 2024, and how much have the banks paid back so far? (This goes in a private claim file only, never in memory.)
2. Do you have your May 2024 statement or a screenshot, plus your repayment emails? Ask them to upload what they have.
3. Which state do you live in, and what time zone? (Used for small claims rules and for scheduling.)
4. Would you like a monthly check of the CFPB pages that tells you only when something changes?
Then save the state and time zone to memory, start the claim file, offer to create the monthly routine (switched off until they say yes), and follow the yotta-recovery-playbook skill.
